cards.title: Set up a first Standard Shopping campaign for bestsellers only
cards.summary: Launch Google Shopping by running only 5-10 bestseller products in a single ad group instead of dumping the whole catalog in one campaign.
cards.use_when: You are creating your first Google Shopping campaign and deciding which products to advertise.
steps: In Google Ads go to Campaigns > plus > Create, choose the Sales objective, and set conversion goals to purchases only (remove add-to-cart and begin-checkout as primary goals so Google doesn't chase the cheaper action). Verify the current interface before relying on exact menu paths.
Choose Shopping as the campaign type and select your linked Merchant Center account/feed; if multiple feeds exist, pick the correct one.
When Google pre-selects Performance Max, switch to Standard Shopping. The source advises avoiding PMAX when the account has no conversion data because it is likely to lose money without data.
Name the campaign consistently (e.g. 'Shopping | USA | Bestsellers | Max Clicks') so the products, geo and bid strategy are obvious.

Pick 5-10 known or predicted bestsellers (under 10 is the source's recommendation). Small catalogs in one campaign get attention spread thin if the budget is limited, and Google may latch onto weak products at mediocre ROAS.
caveats: Source-specific heuristic: 5-10 products, under 10. Not a benchmark.
Menu labels and defaults change; verify in the current UI.

cards.title: Restrict a Shopping ad group to specific products by item ID
cards.summary: Use product group subdivisions and exclusion to make a bestsellers ad group run only the chosen products, not the whole feed.
cards.use_when: Your new Shopping ad group is showing all products and you want it to contain only bestsellers.
steps: Open Campaigns > Ad groups, select the campaign and ad group, then open the Product groups tab.
All products is enabled by default; click the plus to Add subdivision. Prefer subdividing by Item ID when the feed is not cleanly categorized.
Search each bestseller by name, select it, and repeat until all chosen products are listed, then Continue to edit bids and Save (do not change bid values on that screen).
The group now shows your selected products separately plus an 'everything else / all products' row.
Click the green status dot on the all-products row and change it to Exclude, leaving only the selected bestsellers enabled.
caveats: Excluding everything else means only the listed products can serve; re-check the list when you add or retire products.
Category subdivision only works if the Merchant Center feed is consistently categorized.
cards.source_name: Full Ecom Google Ads Course 2026 (100% FREE).docx

cards.title: Choose a Shopping bid strategy based on account conversion data
cards.summary: Start a new Shopping campaign on Maximize Clicks, then graduate to Maximize Conversion Value and target ROAS as conversions accumulate.
cards.use_when: You are setting the bidding strategy for a Shopping campaign and need to decide between clicks and conversion-based bidding.
steps: With no conversion data in the account, select Maximize Clicks. The source states conversion-based bidding on a data-less account tends to perform poorly.
Once roughly 15+ conversions exist, consider switching to Maximize Conversion Value.
At roughly 30+ conversions per month with a consistent ROAS (source example: hovering around 2.5), consider adding a Target ROAS so Google holds performance near the level you were already achieving.
Optional: set a Maximum CPC bid limit only after you know your average CPC from performance columns, to clip outlier bids far above normal (source example: seeing $5 bids when average CPC is $1.20).
caveats: 15 and 30 conversions plus the 2.5 ROAS figure are source-specific heuristics, not established thresholds.
A Max CPC cap set too tight can suppress delivery.
cards.source_name: Full Ecom Google Ads Course 2026 (100% FREE).docx

cards.title: Configure Shopping targeting: presence only, no search partners
cards.summary: Set geo targeting to presence-only, uncheck search network, and use all devices to keep Shopping spend on real in-market buyers.
cards.use_when: You are finalizing locations, networks and devices on a Shopping campaign.
steps: Uncheck the automatically-enabled Search Network option unless you have already fully saturated the Google network (source says leave it off by default).
Set devices to All Devices for most scenarios.

Select the target location (e.g. United States), then open Location options and choose Presence, not Presence or interest. Presence-or-interest can show ads to people outside the country who merely show interest in it.
Leave start and end dates as the creation date unless you have a specific flight.
caveats: Google may still optimize device delivery toward the best-performing devices.
Presence-vs-interest option is absent on some campaign types.
cards.source_name: Full Ecom Google Ads Course 2026 (100% FREE).docx

cards.title: Exclude branded searches from a non-branded Shopping campaign
cards.summary: Add your brand name variations as exact-match negative keywords so your prospecting Shopping campaign stays non-branded.
cards.use_when: You run a Shopping campaign intended for new-customer, non-brand acquisition and want branded traffic excluded.
steps: Go to Campaigns > Audiences, keywords and content > Search keywords, and select the Shopping campaign.
Under Negative search keywords, click plus to add negatives.
Enter all brand-name variations (e.g. 'Peter's Pans', 'Peter's Pans frying pans') as exact match using square brackets so you exclude only those queries and not adjacent traffic.
Keep the campaign's targeting non-branded; branded traffic should be handled in a separate branded campaign.
caveats: Overly broad negatives can strip useful non-brand queries; exact match limits the blast radius.
Source attributes the branded/non-branded separation rationale to its overview module; the concept is that branded and prospecting traffic perform differently and should be measured separately.
cards.source_name: Full Ecom Google Ads Course 2026 (100% FREE).docx

cards.title: Sequence a second all-products Shopping campaign after bestsellers prove out
cards.summary: Once bestsellers deliver consistent sales and ROAS, launch an all-products Shopping campaign with no exclusions to find the next winners.
cards.use_when: Your bestsellers Shopping campaign is producing consistent sales and you want to prospect for additional high-performing products.
steps: Confirm the bestsellers campaign has steady, consistent sales and a stable, profitable ROAS first.
Create a second Shopping campaign using the same setup but skip the product-group subdivision so all products remain enabled.
Run this all-products campaign as a discovery channel to identify more potential bestsellers.
Feed any discovered winners back into the bestsellers campaign structure and remove losers.
caveats: Source says to only do this after bestsellers are working, not at launch.
An all-products campaign can also be run as PMAX, but the source sticks to Shopping for this step.
cards.source_name: Full Ecom Google Ads Course 2026 (100% FREE).docx

cards.title: Prune underperforming products from a bestsellers campaign
cards.summary: Exclude products from the bestsellers campaign that received meaningful spend and clicks but failed to perform.
cards.use_when: A bestsellers Shopping campaign is live and some products are dragging down overall ROAS.
steps: Review product-level performance to find items with substantial ad spend and clicks but weak or unprofitable returns.
Exclude those products from the bestsellers ad group using the product group exclusion flow.
Keep the bestsellers campaign reserved only for products that justify inclusion.
caveats: The source does not give a numeric spend or click threshold; use judgement and enough data before cutting.
Removing a product entirely stops it serving; it can be re-added or moved to the all-products campaign.
cards.source_name: Full Ecom Google Ads Course 2026 (100% FREE).docx

cards.title: Add a low-budget branded Shopping campaign to capture branded product searches
cards.summary: If you have significant branded demand, run an all-products Shopping campaign with a brand-negative script at a small budget to show products for brand searches.
cards.use_when: You have meaningful branded search volume (from ads, organic or other channels) and are not fully capturing it with search campaigns.
steps: Set up a Shopping campaign with the same process as your standard campaign but leave all products enabled and exclude nothing.
Use a small budget sized to cover branded traffic only (source example: around $20/day).
Implement a branded Shopping script (source credits 'PBC masterminds' and provides a link) via Tools > Bulk actions > Scripts, copy the script and make the required modifications.
Verify the current script and its instructions before use, since third-party scripts and the interface change.
caveats: Only needed if you have substantial branded traffic; branded shopping campaigns are optional.
Source says you can also do this even if you simply want your products to appear on brand searches.
cards.source_name: Full Ecom Google Ads Course 2026 (100% FREE).docx

cards.title: Check audience lists and tagging before any remarketing campaign
cards.summary: Ensure the Google Ads tag, GA4 and linked accounts are feeding audience lists, and wait until lists are large enough to target.
cards.use_when: You plan to run any display, video or PMAX remarketing campaign and need working audience data first.
steps: Open Tools > Shared library > Audience manager to see which audiences the account is tracking (some auto-created, some from other sources).
Prioritize the automatic setup: the Google Ads tag, GA4 linked through the data manager, and the Shopify link, which the source calls the easiest and most reliable for most stores.

Consider a customer match import plugin (source names 'Simprosys Custom Match list') to upload Shopify customers into Google Ads and feed purchase-converter data; the source describes it as cheap and optional, not required.
Wait until lists have accumulated enough users before launching remarketing; too-small lists make targeting ineffective.
caveats: Source does not specify a minimum list size, only that small lists won't allow effective targeting.
Plugin names and setup flows change; verify before implementing.
cards.source_name: Full Ecom Google Ads Course 2026 (100% FREE).docx

cards.title: Set up a Display remarketing campaign for returning visitors
cards.summary: Build a low-budget Display campaign targeting all-site visitors with conversion-value bidding and strictly non-expanded targeting.
cards.use_when: You have re-engagement audiences populated and want to retarget past site visitors with Display image ads.
steps: Create a new campaign with Sales objective and purchases-only conversion goals, choose Display, and enter the landing page. Send users to a page designed for prior visitors (offer or deal page) if you have one; otherwise the base or relevant collection page.
Set geo with Presence only, leave most settings at defaults, and start budget low, around $10-15/day. The source warns that high Display budgets can push low-quality placements.

Use conversion-value bidding (Maximize Conversion Value), since remarketing is introduced when the account already has data. Target ROAS can be added later; if enabled early, set a very low target so it doesn't restrict delivery.
In targeting, choose audience segments from your data: Browse > How they've interacted with your business > website visitors, e.g. all users.
Uncheck Optimized Targeting, which is on by default. It expands delivery beyond your remarketing list, which defeats the purpose. The source says it has not performed well for this use.

Build the ad with at least the required landscape and square images; the source considers images more important than headlines/descriptions here. Creative should assume the viewer already knows the brand, e.g. a code offer like 'PETER30 for 30% off' rather than an introduction.
caveats: Source opinion: avoid optimized targeting on remarketing; stated as the presenter's experience, not a universal rule.
Budget figures are source examples, not benchmarks.
cards.source_name: Full Ecom Google Ads Course 2026 (100% FREE).docx

cards.title: Run Video remarketing for site visitors with a product feed attached
cards.summary: Set up a YouTube video remarketing campaign using conversion bidding, tight site-visitor audiences, 3/day frequency cap, and product feed relevance.
cards.use_when: You want a more efficient remarketing channel than Display and are ready to retarget site visitors via YouTube.
steps: Create a campaign with Sales objective, purchases goal, and Video type. Note the source says Video campaigns were being upgraded to Demand Gen in early 2025; verify the current campaign types.
Use Maximize Conversions (source says Maximize Conversion Value is not available on video). Budget around $10-20/day; the source recommends roughly 10-15% of total account budget for remarketing.
Attach a Merchant Center product feed so relevant products show clickable below the ad (e.g. a non-stick pan ad paired with a non-stick pan feed), improving relevance and clickthrough.
Device: if running vertical YouTube Shorts only, target mobile phones; if running landscape and portrait, keep all devices and let Google optimize toward the best performers.
Set frequency capping to about 3 impressions per day. The source argues views beyond that rarely change opinion and waste spend.
Turn off video enhancements so Google doesn't auto-edit or crop your videos; you should know exactly what creative is running.

In the ad group, target all users (or specific segments like product viewers/abandoners), uncheck optimized targeting, and upload your video to YouTube (public or unlisted) and paste its URL. Add a CTA, headline and description, using the preview panels to see how each asset appears.
caveats: Source opinion: video remarketing is typically more efficient than image display remarketing; invest there first, but this is the presenter's observation.
Frequency cap of 3/day is a source recommendation, not a proven threshold.
Video campaign type may no longer exist; verify in the current interface.
cards.source_name: Full Ecom Google Ads Course 2026 (100% FREE).docx

cards.title: Use 2-3 high-quality ad copy assets rather than filling every field
cards.summary: Write fewer, stronger headlines and descriptions in remarketing ads instead of padding out every asset suggestion.
cards.use_when: You are building a Display or Video remarketing ad and Google offers many headline/description slots.
steps: Provide at least one or two headlines and descriptions, which is enough to launch and run a little testing.
Stop there rather than filling every available slot; the source argues you end up populating the later ones with low-quality copy.
Tailor all copy and creative to the specific remarketing segment (all visitors, cart abandoners, product viewers) so it reads as re-engagement, not a first introduction.
If you test asset performance, use separate ads with different assets so you can compare cleanly.
caveats: Source opinion about asset quality versus quantity; not a tested rule.
Minimum required assets still must be supplied for the ad to run.
cards.source_name: Full Ecom Google Ads Course 2026 (100% FREE).docx

cards.title: Position PMAX as a remarketing weapon alongside new-customer Shopping
cards.summary: Use PMAX to retarget Shopping customers with product listings, keeping Shopping as the new-customer acquisition funnel.
cards.use_when: You already have Shopping campaigns acquiring new customers and want a retargeting layer using PMAX.
steps: Keep the Shopping campaign as the new-customer funnel targeting non-branded searches (branded traffic excluded via negatives).
Set up a PMAX campaign whose strategic purpose is to retarget those shopping customers with shopping listings and high-intent ads.
Get the important PMAX settings right before launching; the source stresses that PMAX is very data- and algorithm-dependent and can waste money when not contained by the correct strategy.
Treat PMAX as reliant on existing account data, consistent with the source's advice to avoid using it at the outset when there is no data.
caveats: Source describes this PMAX-as-remarketing approach as a fairly new, specific strategy; the full PMAX settings walkthrough is in a later module, not this section.
Source states PMAX set up wrongly wastes money, and without data is likely to lose money.
